title: Subqueries in WHERE
description: A subquery is a complete SELECT nested inside another query - here, inside a WHERE clause, to filter using a value you don't already know. Write a query that returns the `name` and `price` of every product priced above the average price of all products.
hints: You need the average price before you can compare anything to it - (SELECT AVG(price) FROM products) is a complete query on its own, and SQL lets you drop it right inside another query's WHERE clause in place of a literal number.
SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price > (a subquery computing AVG(price) FROM products).
expected_behavior: Returns name and price for products whose price exceeds the average price across all products.
solution: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price > (SELECT AVG(price) FROM products);
explanation: A subquery in WHERE runs first, produces a single value, and the outer query then compares each row against it - the database handles the ordering, you just nest the query where the value belongs.
